cards.explanation: The answer is so the Son may glorify the Father. Jesus asks, “Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You.” Look at where that lands, friends. The honor goes right back to the Father. Jesus asks, and the Father ends up with the glory.

The answer is eternal life. Jesus says the Father granted Him authority over all people “…so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.” That's the gift the verse names. It's a good one, friends. Eternal life is what Jesus gives.

The answer is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ. Jesus says, “Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.” He explains eternal life as knowing the Father and the Son. That's the whole definition He gives right there in the prayer.
The answer is work. Jesus says, “I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.” The Father gave Him work, and He accomplished it. Nice and plain.

The answer is False. Jesus asks the Father, “…glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” Look at that word "had." He isn't asking for something brand new, friends. He's asking to be back in the Father's presence with the glory that was already His, like a stamper asking for his own spot on the counter.
The answer is kept. Jesus says of the disciples, “They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.” They kept it. Hold onto that word, friends, because it's the one Jesus uses.

The answer is that Jesus came from the Father. Jesus says, “They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.” That's what they knew for sure. They had received the words He gave them, and they knew where He came from.

The answer is the world. Jesus says, “I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me; for they are Yours.” Here He's asking on behalf of the ones the Father gave Him. The world is the one He names as not included in this request.

The answer is so they may be one. Jesus says, “Holy Father, protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.” Protection comes with a purpose, and the purpose is oneness. That word is going to come up again before this prayer is over.

The answer is lost. Jesus says, “Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.” He protected and preserved them by the Father's name. Lost is the word He uses.

The answer is the Scripture. Jesus says the son of destruction was lost “…so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.” He doesn't say which Scripture in this prayer, so I won't guess. He just says Scripture, and that's where we stop.

The answer is so His joy may be fulfilled in them. Jesus says, “…I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.” He's still in the world as He prays. The reason He gives is joy, and it's His joy.

The answer is that it has hated them. Jesus says, “I have given them Your word and the world has hated them.” He tells it to the Father straight. And He follows it with, “For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.”

The answer is that the Father keep them from the evil one. Jesus says, “I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.” He isn't asking for them to be taken out of the world. His request is that the Father keep them from the evil one.
The answer is word. Jesus says, “Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.” He is asking the Father to sanctify them by the truth. And He says the Father's word is truth.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.” The Father sent Jesus, and Jesus has sent the disciples. It's the same kind of sending, said in one line.

The answer is those who will believe through their message. Jesus says, “I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message…” The prayer reaches past the disciples to people who believe through their message. That's a wide circle, friends, and Jesus prays for it.

The answer is so the world may believe the Father sent Him. Jesus prays, “May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.” Oneness is tied to the world believing. That's the reason He gives.

The answer is True. Jesus prays for them to be perfectly united “…so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.” There are two things for the world to know. The Father sent Jesus, and the Father has loved them just as He has loved Jesus.

The answer is to be with Him where He is. Jesus says, “Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me…” He wants them with Him. He also wants them to see His glory.

The answer is False. Jesus says the Father gave Him glory “…because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.” The Father's love didn't start when Jesus came into the world. It was there before the foundation of the world.
The answer is False. Jesus says, “…I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known…” Past and future in one breath. He has done it, and He will keep doing it.

The answer is so the Father's love for Him may be in them. Jesus says He'll keep making the name known “…so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.” The Father's love for Jesus in them, and Jesus in them. That's how the prayer ends. And that wraps up the Last Supper, friends.
